milestones are this map's children, vocabulary is the *Context* page (CLO-4) and decisions are the *Decisions* page

- The dev daemon runs from `.cloisters-dev` on port 7227, not 7228 as the plan said (Saqib, 2026-11-12).

title: Context
body:
# Context

Domain vocabulary for cloisters. A glossary, not a spec: no implementation details, no
decisions. Decisions live on [the map](.wayfinder/MAP.md); architecture lives in ADRs.

## Project

A namespace for issues and pages. Owns a short key (`CLO`), the one sequence that numbers
both its issues and its pages, and one page tree. Projects do not nest and carry no configuration — they exist to
scope ids and nothing else.

There is no separate *space*: where Confluence would say "the CLO space", cloisters says
"the CLO project's pages".

A key is 2–10 characters: an uppercase letter, then uppercase letters or digits (`CLO`,
`WF2`).

A project's key is permanent and a project is never removed: the key is part of every
issue id ever issued. Its display name is just a label and may change.

### Bound project

The project a working context means when it names none — a repository directory, or an
agent's connection to cloisters. Binding is set once, outside any conversation. Binding a
context to a project never creates the project. Naming a
project explicitly always overrides it; with no binding, nothing is assumed.

## Issue

The unit of work. One of cloisters' two substantial entities, beside the page. An issue has a title, a
markdown body, a status, labels, an assignee, an optional parent, blocking edges,
comments, and timestamps.

There are no issue *types* — no epic, story, bug, or task. Labels carry every semantic
distinction, which keeps cloisters ignorant of the vocabulary of whatever is using it.

### Issue id

A project key plus a monotonic integer: `CLO-42`. Assigned once, never reused, never
changed. Numbers increase in creation order; they are not promised to be gapless. Chosen to be speakable aloud and typeable into a command line.

Issues and pages draw from the same sequence, so an id names exactly one thing, issue or
page, and the id alone does not say which. Asking for a page as an issue, or the reverse,
is refused by saying what the id actually names.

### Version

A counter on each issue that moves only when its title, body or labels change. A writer
may state the version it last read; if the issue has moved on, the write is refused
rather than silently overwriting. Claims, comments, status changes and edges do not move
it — they have their own guards, or never conflict.

A page has a version too, and it is simply its latest revision number: only title and body
changes move it. The web UI's page editor always states the version it loaded, so a human
never silently overwrites an agent's edit; a stale save is refused and the human merges by
hand.

## Page

A wiki document: a title and a markdown body, belonging to one project's **page tree**.
A page has at most one parent page and any number of child pages; pages without a parent
are the tree's roots. A page tree never crosses projects.

A page is knowledge, not work: it has no status, assignee, claim or blocking edges. Pages
carry no labels and take no comments: to discuss a page, open an issue that mentions it.

A page is identified like an issue: an id such as `CLO-57`, from its project's sequence.
Its title is only a label — titles need not be unique — and a page never moves to another
project, since its id carries the key.

Siblings are ordered by **rank**, as issues are, defaulting to the page's number. A page
**moves** by taking a new parent, or none; it keeps its rank unless the move sets one, and
it can never move beneath itself.

### Archived

A page is either **live** or **archived**. Archiving is how a page leaves the way, since
pages, like issues, are never deleted. An archived page keeps its identity, its history,
and the links to and from it; it is only left out of the page tree and of search unless
asked for. Archiving is reversible. Links to an archived page still resolve, marked as
archived so a reader knows the page is stale.

A live page never has an archived parent. So a page with live children cannot be
archived — the refusal names them; archive or move the children first, and nothing
disappears as a side effect — and no page can be unarchived, moved or created beneath an
archived parent.

### Revision

A saved state of a page's content: its title and body. Every save that changes either makes
a new revision; revisions are never edited or removed, so a page's history can always be
read, compared, and an earlier revision restored — restoring makes a new revision, it does
not rewind, and the new revision records which one it restored. Revisions are numbered per
page (`CLO-57` r3).

A revision is not a second record beside the timeline: it is the page as it stood after an
event that changed its content. Moving, reordering and archiving are events on the page's
timeline but make no revision, so restoring puts back only what the page said. An archived page can
still be edited: archiving hides a page, it does not lock it.

### Edit summary

A short note on why a page changed, given with the write and kept on its event. Optional
when editing; required when archiving or unarchiving, as closing and reopening an issue
always say why. It is not a comment: pages take no comments.

### Mentions of pages

Pages are mentioned exactly as issues are — see **Mention** — so there is no separate
kind of page link. Backlinks run in both directions: an issue lists the pages that
mention it, and a page lists the issues and pages that mention it.

## Status

Exactly two values: `open` and `closed`. Nothing else is a status.

**In progress** is not a status. It is *derived*: an open issue with an assignee is in
progress. This is a deliberate refusal — a stored in-progress flag can drift out of
agreement with the assignee, and a derived one cannot.

**Reopening** returns a closed issue to open, discarding its resolution (the timeline
keeps it). Like closing, it always carries a comment saying why.

Issues are never deleted. Closing as `dropped` is the only way out, including for issues
created by mistake.

## Resolution

Recorded when an issue is closed. Either `done` (the work was carried out) or `dropped`
(the issue was closed without being carried out — abandoned, obsolete, or ruled outside
the scope of the effort).

The distinction matters because "we finished this" and "we decided not to" are different
facts about the route taken, and a single closed status loses the difference.

Closing always carries a comment saying why. A resolution records *what* happened; the
comment records the reasoning a later reader will need.

## Assignee

Free text naming whoever or whatever holds the issue. Not a reference to a user entity —
cloisters has no users. An agent session and a human are the same kind of thing here.

The assignee names the *holder*, which for parallel work is a session, not a person: two
sessions driven by the same developer claim as distinct names (`saqib/wf-7f3a`). A name shared
between concurrent holders defeats the claim, since claiming what you already hold succeeds.

## Claim

Taking an issue by setting its assignee, conditional on it having none. A claim
**fails** rather than overwrites when the issue is already assigned, which is what makes
it safe for concurrent sessions to race for the same work. Claiming an issue you already
hold is not a conflict: it succeeds and changes nothing.

An open issue with no assignee is **unclaimed**.

The assignee changes only by claiming, releasing, or reassigning — each conditional on
who holds it now:

- **Release** — the holder gives the issue up.
- **Reassign** — someone other than the holder moves the issue on, naming the holder they
  expect to displace. Reassigning to nobody clears the claim.

A **stale claim** is one held long enough that its holder has probably gone — typically an
agent session that ended mid-work. Claims never lapse on their own; a stale claim stays
until someone reassigns it.

A closed issue's assignee is history — the record of who resolved it — so a closed issue
cannot be claimed, released or reassigned. Reopen it first if the work is live again.

## Comment

A remark appended to an issue. Comments are only ever added, never edited or removed, so
two writers can never conflict over one.

## Edges

Exactly three kinds of relationship between issues. Parent and blocks edges only connect
issues in the same project; mentions may reach across projects.

### Parent

Structural hierarchy. An issue has at most one parent and any number of **children**.
Hand-set. Carries containment, not sequencing — a parent is not blocked by its children.

### Blocks

An issue **blocks** another when the second cannot proceed until the first is closed.
Hand-set, many-to-many, and acyclic: writes that would form a cycle are rejected.

An issue is **blocked** while any issue blocking it is still open, and **unblocked**
once all of them are closed.

### Mention

A reference to an id occurring in prose: an issue's title, body or comments, or a page's
title or body. The id may name an issue or a page. Mentions are **derived**, not
curated: writing `CLO-42` in prose creates the edge, and whatever `CLO-42` names gains a
**backlink**. There is no way to hand-author or hand-remove a mention.

An id is written bare (`CLO-42`) or as a link to it (`[the glossary](/CLO-42)`). There is
no link by title: titles change, ids don't.

Only prose counts: an id inside code — an inline code span or a code block — is not a
mention, so pasted logs and code don't create backlinks. An id counts only when its
project exists; it may name something that doesn't exist yet, and becomes a live backlink
when that issue or page is created. Nothing mentions itself.

A mention reflects the current text: editing an id out of a title or body removes the
backlink. Comments are never edited, so a mention in a comment is permanent.

This is the whole of cloisters' "see also". Curated link types — *relates to*, *duplicates*,
*clones* — are deliberately absent; they go stale because nothing forces them to stay
true, whereas a derived edge cannot disagree with the text that produced it.

## Label

An opaque string attached to an issue. Cloisters attaches no meaning to any label and
interprets none of them, including namespaced ones like `wayfinder:map`. Meaning belongs
to whoever is reading.

Labels are case-insensitive: `Bug` and `bug` are the same label.

## Rank

The position of an issue in a total order, or of a page among its siblings. It defaults
to the issue's or page's number, so order is deterministic without anyone setting it, and
can be overwritten to reorder.

Rank is not priority. Cloisters has no priority.

A rank is any decimal number, so an issue or page can be placed between two others (3.5 sits
between 3 and 4) without moving either.

Ranks need not be unique; equal ranks are ordered by number.

## Event

A record that something about an issue or page changed: who, when, which field, and from what to
what. Events accumulate and are never edited or removed, forming an issue's or page's **timeline**.

An issue's or page's current state is the authority on what is true now; the timeline is the record
of how it got there. They are separate on purpose.

One write is one event, however many fields it changes; a comment given with the write
belongs to that event, as does a page's edit summary. A write that changes nothing records no event.

An event belongs to the issue or page written to, and also appears on the timeline of every
issue or page whose parent or blocking edges it changed, or that it unblocked or blocked
again. Closing a blocker shows on each dependent it frees; moving a page shows on its old
and new parent. A **mention** does not carry an event onto the mentioned issue or page —
the backlink appears, the timeline stays quiet.

The event names **who** by the surface and client that made the write (an agent through
MCP, the CLI, the web UI), not by a person.

An issue's or page's **updated** time is the time of the latest event on its timeline — a comment or
a claim updates an issue as much as a title change does.

## Ready

An issue is **ready** when it is open, unblocked, and unclaimed — work anyone could take
right now.

Consumers may have their own word for a scoped slice of ready work (wayfinder calls its
version the *frontier*); cloisters does not adopt those words.

title: Decisions
body:
Architecture decisions for cloisters, one child page per decision. Before the dogfood point they lived in
`docs/adr/` (now frozen); write new ones as child pages here.

Most decisions are not ADRs: they are the resolved tickets of the planning map (`.wayfinder/tickets/`, and tikka's in
`docs/inherited/tickets/`), which stay in git as history. The build follows the *Build plan* (CLO-7).

title: ADR 0001: Hand-roll MCP as a Ring handler
body:
# Hand-roll MCP as a Ring handler instead of adopting a library

Status: accepted, 2026-10-25.

MCP is cloisters' primary interface, and its contract needs both the stateless 2026-07-28 revision (which Claude Code
negotiates) and 2025-11-25, tool handlers that see the request URL and client name, and `isError` results carrying
`structuredContent`. As of October 2026 no Clojure library speaks 2026-07-28 (PluMCP 0.3.0 lists it as TODO;
roklenarcic/mcp-server 0.3.61 is alpha and quiet), and the only JVM implementation that does, the Java SDK's 2.2.0-M1
milestone, is a servlet plus Reactor that mounts beside a Ring stack, not inside it. So cloisters implements MCP itself:
a Ring handler at `/mcp` from JSON-RPC request maps to response maps, JSON responses only, tools only, with the official
conformance suite run in CI at both revisions as the safety net. Tikka's equivalent was about 200 lines.

## Consequences

Cloisters owns spec drift: each new revision is its own work, and the conformance suite says when it falls behind.
That stays cheap only while the contract refuses everything hard in MCP (resources, prompts, sampling, elicitation,
tasks, subscriptions, auth).

**Revisit when** a Clojure MCP library supports both current revisions, gives tool handlers the request and client
info, and publishes conformance results (PluMCP is the likeliest), or when the contract grows beyond tools.

title: Build plan
body:
# Build plan

The planning map ([.wayfinder/MAP.md](../.wayfinder/MAP.md)) is complete: every decision lives in exactly one
resolved ticket, either a cloisters ticket or an inherited tikka ticket that carries over. This plan only **orders**
the build. It restates no decision: each milestone names the tickets it implements, and those tickets are the spec.
The ordering itself was decided in [Write the build plan](../.wayfinder/tickets/T15-build-plan.md).

**Read tickets to the end.** Several carry *Amended by* notes below their resolution, and those notes override the
text above them. The walking skeleton's amendments matter most. Read inherited tickets with "tikka" as "cloisters"
and `TIK` as `CLO`; where a cloisters ticket re-decides something, the cloisters ticket wins.

Every milestone covers **issues and pages together**. The shared id space, cross-kind mentions and one `search` make
a later "pages milestone" a second pass through every layer.

## Working rules

- **Start clean.** The [walking skeleton branch](https://github.com/saqib-trywe/cloisters/tree/prototype/walking-skeleton)
  is reference. Write new code, except for files you can copy verbatim after review: the vendored `htmx.min.js`
  (4.0.0), the jsdom shims in `scripts/ui-test.js`, `paths.clj`, and the lock and migration runner.
- **Branches.** One branch per milestone (`build/m0-scaffold`, `build/m1-store`, …), always branched from `main`,
  never stacked on the previous milestone. Each merges to `main` by squash PR once CI is green. `main` only ever
  holds working milestones. The ProtectMainCloisters ruleset requires a review a solo author cannot give, so PRs merge
  with `--admin` once CI is green.
- **Sessions.** Start each milestone in a fresh session.
- **Done** means the milestone's checks pass, not that its code is written.
- **Staging.** Stage explicit paths only; never commit build artifacts (`target/`, `.cpcache/`, `node_modules/`,
  `.cloisters-dev/`).
- **Conventions** live in a root `CLAUDE.md`, written in M0. Vocabulary lives in [CONTEXT.md](../CONTEXT.md).
- **Research inline.** Verify library facts from Maven Central or Clojars metadata and release notes, not docs pages.

## CI

GitHub Actions runs on `ubuntu-latest` and `macos-latest`. A gate switches on in the milestone that creates the
thing it tests, and stays on after that:

| Gate | From |
|---|---|
| clj-kondo, cljfmt check, test-runner | M0 |
| Tests against a real temporary SQLite file, including migrating a non-empty store | M1 |
| MCP conformance `0.2.0-alpha.12` with `--requirements` at both revisions, against the `--expected-failures` baseline (installed in M0) | M4 |
| CLI startup gate: `cloisters search` under 100 ms against a live daemon | M5 |
| jsdom UI check against a live daemon, with the htmx 4 shims | M6 |

## Milestones

### M0: Scaffold and CI

- Root `deps.edn` and a tools.build uberjar for the daemon.
- The babashka CLI at `cli/cloisters.clj`.
- cognitect-labs test-runner, clj-kondo and cljfmt.
- `mise.toml` pins JDK 27, the Clojure CLI, babashka and node.
- `CLAUDE.md` carries the Clojure conventions, the skeleton's build conventions and the shell quirks (see below).
- CI installs the pinned conformance suite; its scenarios first run in M4.

Implements: [Survey the Clojure ecosystem for cloisters](../.wayfinder/tickets/T01-clojure-ecosystem-survey.md),
[Choose the CLI approach](../.wayfinder/tickets/T09-cli-approach.md) (tooling only),
[Walking skeleton](../.wayfinder/tickets/T13-walking-skeleton.md) (its findings table).

**Done when:** CI runs lint, format and an empty test suite green on both platforms.

### M1: Store and lifecycle

- Paths: XDG locations, plus the `CLOISTERS_HOME` override.
- EDN config and the daemon lock.
- The hand-rolled `user_version` migration runner, with `VACUUM INTO` snapshots and `quick_check`.
- Schema v1:
  - the `item` table enforcing the shared id space
  - projects, issues, and pages with parent, sibling rank and archive
  - stored revisions, labels, parent and blocking edges, mentions carrying kind, events with changes
  - one FTS5 table over both kinds
- HikariCP readers plus one locked writer.

Implements: [Choose the persistence stack](../.wayfinder/tickets/T06-persistence-stack.md),
[Place cloisters' files in the XDG base directories](../.wayfinder/tickets/T03-xdg-file-locations.md); inherited
[Choose the persistence engine](inherited/tickets/T03-persistence-engine.md),
[Daemon lifecycle and repo-to-project binding](inherited/tickets/T10-daemon-lifecycle.md) (lock, migrations),
[Decide export and durability](inherited/tickets/T17-export-and-durability.md) (snapshots, integrity),
[Define the event log schema](inherited/tickets/T14-event-log-schema.md) (tables).

**Done when:** real-SQLite tests show a second daemon refused by the lock, a non-empty store migrated with its
snapshot reopening at the old version, and one id sequence shared by issues and pages.

### M2: Core

- Every invariant, with rejections that name the conflict.
- Compare-and-set claims, decimal ranks, versions, and one event per write (none when nothing changes).
- Page revisions and the `stale_version` guard; archive, unarchive and restore, with `archived_parent` and
  `live_children`; diff.
- Mention detection: code never counts, forward references, project rescans, backlinks in both directions.
- The export function, which writes `page` records and page events carrying their revision.

Implements: [Amend scope and shape for the wiki](../.wayfinder/tickets/T02-amend-scope-for-the-wiki.md),
[Define page identity and linking](../.wayfinder/tickets/T04-page-identity-and-linking.md),
[Define page revisions and edit conflicts](../.wayfinder/tickets/T05-page-revisions-and-conflicts.md),
[Extend export and durability to pages](../.wayfinder/tickets/T14-export-and-durability-for-pages.md); inherited
[Define tikka's core invariants](inherited/tickets/T02-core-invariants.md),
[Define the event log schema](inherited/tickets/T14-event-log-schema.md),
[Settle body and mention conventions](inherited/tickets/T15-body-and-mention-conventions.md),
[Decide export and durability](inherited/tickets/T17-export-and-durability.md) (export).

**Done when:** real-store tests pass for:

- every invariant
- the concurrent claim race
- page moves, archiving and restoring
- stale page edits
- forward mentions and project rescans
- a deterministic export

### M3: Query grammar and search

- The parser with suggestions, compiled through HoneySQL.
- `kind:` (implied by kind-only filters), with `archived:no` as the default.
- Full-text search over both kinds.
- Keyset cursors and sorts.
- `assignee:` prefix matching.
- Recent changes and page trees, expressed as queries.

Implements: [Extend the query grammar and search to pages](../.wayfinder/tickets/T12-query-grammar-for-pages.md);
inherited [Define the shared query and filter grammar](inherited/tickets/T08-query-grammar.md),
[Confirm wayfinder fits tikka's contract](inherited/tickets/T16-wayfinder-fits-tikka.md).

**Done when:** tests cover every row of the grammar's filter table, including the page filters.

### M4: HTTP and MCP

- HTTP adapter:
  - Ring on Jetty, reitit routing, one jsonista mapper for both JSON edges (nulls dropped), and the malli contract
    validated by the core
  - adapter catch-alls and localhost hardening
  - REST plus intent actions, including `/api/pages`; `Accept: text/plain`; `/api/meta`
  - the event feed and resumable SSE stream, which opens with a comment
- MCP adapter:
  - the hand-rolled JSON-RPC Ring handler at `/mcp`, at 2025-11-25 and 2026-07-28
  - all sixteen tools, rendered by the shared text renderer

Implements: [Define the shared contract and HTTP adapter](../.wayfinder/tickets/T10-shared-contract-and-http.md),
[Choose the MCP implementation](../.wayfinder/tickets/T07-mcp-implementation.md) and
[ADR 0001](adr/0001-hand-rolled-mcp.md),
[Extend the MCP tool contract for pages](../.wayfinder/tickets/T11-mcp-tools-for-pages.md); inherited
[Design the HTTP API shape](inherited/tickets/T09-http-api-shape.md),
[Design the MCP tool contract](inherited/tickets/T07-mcp-tool-contract.md),
[Choose the MCP server implementation and transport](inherited/tickets/T04-mcp-implementation.md).

**Done when:**

- conformance at both revisions matches the baseline in CI
- a test validates every tool result against its own declared schema
- a real Claude Code session completes claim → edit → close on an issue, and create → update → archive on a page

### Dogfood point

Move the rest of the build, and the planning documents, into cloisters itself. From here, work goes through
cloisters' own MCP surface.

- **Daemon.**
  - `CLOISTERS_HOME=.cloisters-dev/` inside the repo (gitignored), on port **7227** (amended 2026-11-12: Saqib keeps the dev instance as his only cloisters, so it takes the default port; the plan said 7228, to keep 7227 and the XDG locations
    stay free for a real install). tikka keeps 7117.
  - It runs from a jar copied into `.cloisters-dev/`; after each milestone merge, copy the new jar and restart.
  - Kill scratch daemons by the pid in their lock, never by pattern.
- **Binding.** Create project `CLO`. Bind the repository through `.cloisters` and a project-scoped `.mcp.json`
  entry. Put the daemon's start command in `CLAUDE.md`.
- **Issues.** A map issue, *Build cloisters' first release*, with M5 and M6 as its children, worked wayfinder-style
  per [Confirm wayfinder fits tikka's contract](inherited/tickets/T16-wayfinder-fits-tikka.md).
- **Pages.**
  - a *Context* page, from `CONTEXT.md`
  - a *Decisions* page with one child page per ADR
  - a *Build plan* page, from this file
  - The build plan page mentions the milestone issues, and each milestone issue mentions the pages it implements, so
    mentions work in both directions.
- **Repo copies.**
  - `CONTEXT.md`, `docs/adr/` and this file are frozen, each with a header naming its page: "Superseded at the
    dogfood point by CLO-n; edit the page."
  - `CLAUDE.md` tells sessions to read vocabulary through `get_page`, and new ADRs are written as pages.
  - `.wayfinder/` and `docs/inherited/` stay untouched as history.
- **Durability.** Commit the export's output as `docs/dogfood-export.jsonl` with each milestone merge. It is a
  readable record; it cannot restore anything, because cloisters has no import.

**Reached when:** a fresh Claude Code session in this repository finds the map issue's frontier, reads the *Context*
page, and sees backlinks in both directions.

### M5: CLI

- Every command, plus the `page` verbs, shared `show`/`edit`, and the `$EDITOR` flow, where a refused edit keeps the
  file.
- Bulk close, `project new` and `init`.
- The `daemon` subcommands: install, run, start, stop, status, logs, export, restore.
- The `cloisters mcp` stdio proxy.
- Installed by `bbin`, which copies the script: reinstall after every change. babashka must be installed user-wide,
  not only through the repo's `mise.toml`.

Implements: [Choose the CLI approach](../.wayfinder/tickets/T09-cli-approach.md); inherited
[Daemon lifecycle and repo-to-project binding](inherited/tickets/T10-daemon-lifecycle.md),
[Decide export and durability](inherited/tickets/T17-export-and-durability.md).

**Done when:** the 100 ms gate is green in CI, and `cloisters init` plus Claude Code works end to end in a fresh
repository.

### M6: Web UI

- Server-rendered hiccup with htmx 4.0.0 (vendored), as a thin adapter over the core.
- Issue views: ready, tree and detail.
- Page views: tree, page view, the plain markdown editor with preview, the always-on guard and hand merge, diff, and
  recent changes.
- Live updates over the one SSE stream, and inline edits.
- The safe nextjournal/markdown renderer, with mentions linked.

Implements: [Choose the web UI approach](../.wayfinder/tickets/T08-web-ui-approach.md),
[Define page revisions and edit conflicts](../.wayfinder/tickets/T05-page-revisions-and-conflicts.md) (the editor);
inherited [Settle body and mention conventions](inherited/tickets/T15-body-and-mention-conventions.md).

**Done when:** the jsdom check is green in CI, and Saqib confirms a browser walkthrough of every view and edit.

## Build conventions from the skeleton

These go into `CLAUDE.md` in M0. The detail is in
[Walking skeleton](../.wayfinder/tickets/T13-walking-skeleton.md).

- Write malli schemas with `mu/merge`, not `:merge`. Write titles as a single `:re`, not
  `[:and :string [:re …]]`.
- In HoneySQL raw fragments, bind parameters with `[:lift x]`; `RETURNING` allocates ids.

# Context

Domain vocabulary for cloisters. A glossary, not a spec: no implementation details, no
decisions. Decisions live on [the map](.wayfinder/MAP.md); architecture lives in ADRs.

## Project

A namespace for issues and pages. Owns a short key (`CLO`), the one sequence that numbers
both its issues and its pages, and one page tree. Projects do not nest and carry no configuration — they exist to
scope ids and nothing else.

There is no separate *space*: where Confluence would say "the CLO space", cloisters says
"the CLO project's pages".

A key is 2–10 characters: an uppercase letter, then uppercase letters or digits (`CLO`,
`WF2`).

A project's key is permanent and a project is never removed: the key is part of every
issue id ever issued. Its display name is just a label and may change.

### Bound project

The project a working context means when it names none — a repository directory, or an
agent's connection to cloisters. Binding is set once, outside any conversation. Binding a
context to a project never creates the project. Naming a
project explicitly always overrides it; with no binding, nothing is assumed.

## Issue

The unit of work. One of cloisters' two substantial entities, beside the page. An issue has a title, a
markdown body, a status, labels, an assignee, an optional parent, blocking edges,
comments, and timestamps.

There are no issue *types* — no epic, story, bug, or task. Labels carry every semantic
distinction, which keeps cloisters ignorant of the vocabulary of whatever is using it.

### Issue id

A project key plus a monotonic integer: `CLO-42`. Assigned once, never reused, never
changed. Numbers increase in creation order; they are not promised to be gapless. Chosen to be speakable aloud and typeable into a command line.

Issues and pages draw from the same sequence, so an id names exactly one thing, issue or
page, and the id alone does not say which. Asking for a page as an issue, or the reverse,
is refused by saying what the id actually names.

### Version

A counter on each issue that moves only when its title, body or labels change. A writer
may state the version it last read; if the issue has moved on, the write is refused
rather than silently overwriting. Claims, comments, status changes and edges do not move
it — they have their own guards, or never conflict.

A page has a version too, and it is simply its latest revision number: only title and body
changes move it. The web UI's page editor always states the version it loaded, so a human
never silently overwrites an agent's edit; a stale save is refused and the human merges by
hand.

## Page

A wiki document: a title and a markdown body, belonging to one project's **page tree**.
A page has at most one parent page and any number of child pages; pages without a parent
are the tree's roots. A page tree never crosses projects.

A page is knowledge, not work: it has no status, assignee, claim or blocking edges. Pages
carry no labels and take no comments: to discuss a page, open an issue that mentions it.

A page is identified like an issue: an id such as `CLO-57`, from its project's sequence.
Its title is only a label — titles need not be unique — and a page never moves to another
project, since its id carries the key.

Siblings are ordered by **rank**, as issues are, defaulting to the page's number. A page
**moves** by taking a new parent, or none; it keeps its rank unless the move sets one, and
it can never move beneath itself.

### Archived

A page is either **live** or **archived**. Archiving is how a page leaves the way, since
pages, like issues, are never deleted. An archived page keeps its identity, its history,
and the links to and from it; it is only left out of the page tree and of search unless
asked for. Archiving is reversible. Links to an archived page still resolve, marked as
archived so a reader knows the page is stale.

A live page never has an archived parent. So a page with live children cannot be
archived — the refusal names them; archive or move the children first, and nothing
disappears as a side effect — and no page can be unarchived, moved or created beneath an
archived parent.

### Revision

A saved state of a page's content: its title and body. Every save that changes either makes
a new revision; revisions are never edited or removed, so a page's history can always be
read, compared, and an earlier revision restored — restoring makes a new revision, it does
not rewind, and the new revision records which one it restored. Revisions are numbered per
page (`CLO-57` r3).

A revision is not a second record beside the timeline: it is the page as it stood after an
event that changed its content. Moving, reordering and archiving are events on the page's
timeline but make no revision, so restoring puts back only what the page said. An archived page can
still be edited: archiving hides a page, it does not lock it.

### Edit summary

A short note on why a page changed, given with the write and kept on its event. Optional
when editing; required when archiving or unarchiving, as closing and reopening an issue
always say why. It is not a comment: pages take no comments.

### Mentions of pages

Pages are mentioned exactly as issues are — see **Mention** — so there is no separate
kind of page link. Backlinks run in both directions: an issue lists the pages that
mention it, and a page lists the issues and pages that mention it.

## Status

Exactly two values: `open` and `closed`. Nothing else is a status.

**In progress** is not a status. It is *derived*: an open issue with an assignee is in
progress. This is a deliberate refusal — a stored in-progress flag can drift out of
agreement with the assignee, and a derived one cannot.

**Reopening** returns a closed issue to open, discarding its resolution (the timeline
keeps it). Like closing, it always carries a comment saying why.

Issues are never deleted. Closing as `dropped` is the only way out, including for issues
created by mistake.

## Resolution

Recorded when an issue is closed. Either `done` (the work was carried out) or `dropped`
(the issue was closed without being carried out — abandoned, obsolete, or ruled outside
the scope of the effort).

The distinction matters because "we finished this" and "we decided not to" are different
facts about the route taken, and a single closed status loses the difference.

Closing always carries a comment saying why. A resolution records *what* happened; the
comment records the reasoning a later reader will need.

## Assignee

Free text naming whoever or whatever holds the issue. Not a reference to a user entity —
cloisters has no users. An agent session and a human are the same kind of thing here.

The assignee names the *holder*, which for parallel work is a session, not a person: two
sessions driven by the same developer claim as distinct names (`saqib/wf-7f3a`). A name shared
between concurrent holders defeats the claim, since claiming what you already hold succeeds.

## Claim

Taking an issue by setting its assignee, conditional on it having none. A claim
**fails** rather than overwrites when the issue is already assigned, which is what makes
it safe for concurrent sessions to race for the same work. Claiming an issue you already
hold is not a conflict: it succeeds and changes nothing.

An open issue with no assignee is **unclaimed**.

The assignee changes only by claiming, releasing, or reassigning — each conditional on
who holds it now:

- **Release** — the holder gives the issue up.
- **Reassign** — someone other than the holder moves the issue on, naming the holder they
  expect to displace. Reassigning to nobody clears the claim.

A **stale claim** is one held long enough that its holder has probably gone — typically an
agent session that ended mid-work. Claims never lapse on their own; a stale claim stays
until someone reassigns it.

A closed issue's assignee is history — the record of who resolved it — so a closed issue
cannot be claimed, released or reassigned. Reopen it first if the work is live again.

## Comment

A remark appended to an issue. Comments are only ever added, never edited or removed, so
two writers can never conflict over one.

## Edges

Exactly three kinds of relationship between issues. Parent and blocks edges only connect
issues in the same project; mentions may reach across projects.

### Parent

Structural hierarchy. An issue has at most one parent and any number of **children**.
Hand-set. Carries containment, not sequencing — a parent is not blocked by its children.

### Blocks

An issue **blocks** another when the second cannot proceed until the first is closed.
Hand-set, many-to-many, and acyclic: writes that would form a cycle are rejected.

An issue is **blocked** while any issue blocking it is still open, and **unblocked**
once all of them are closed.

### Mention

A reference to an id occurring in prose: an issue's title, body or comments, or a page's
title or body. The id may name an issue or a page. Mentions are **derived**, not
curated: writing `CLO-42` in prose creates the edge, and whatever `CLO-42` names gains a
**backlink**. There is no way to hand-author or hand-remove a mention.

An id is written bare (`CLO-42`) or as a link to it (`[the glossary](/CLO-42)`). There is
no link by title: titles change, ids don't.

Only prose counts: an id inside code — an inline code span or a code block — is not a
mention, so pasted logs and code don't create backlinks. An id counts only when its
project exists; it may name something that doesn't exist yet, and becomes a live backlink
when that issue or page is created. Nothing mentions itself.

A mention reflects the current text: editing an id out of a title or body removes the
backlink. Comments are never edited, so a mention in a comment is permanent.

This is the whole of cloisters' "see also". Curated link types — *relates to*, *duplicates*,
*clones* — are deliberately absent; they go stale because nothing forces them to stay
true, whereas a derived edge cannot disagree with the text that produced it.

## Label

An opaque string attached to an issue. Cloisters attaches no meaning to any label and
interprets none of them, including namespaced ones like `wayfinder:map`. Meaning belongs
to whoever is reading.

Labels are case-insensitive: `Bug` and `bug` are the same label.

## Rank

The position of an issue in a total order, or of a page among its siblings. It defaults
to the issue's or page's number, so order is deterministic without anyone setting it, and
can be overwritten to reorder.

Rank is not priority. Cloisters has no priority.

A rank is any decimal number, so an issue or page can be placed between two others (3.5 sits
between 3 and 4) without moving either.

Ranks need not be unique; equal ranks are ordered by number.

## Event

A record that something about an issue or page changed: who, when, which field, and from what to
what. Events accumulate and are never edited or removed, forming an issue's or page's **timeline**.

An issue's or page's current state is the authority on what is true now; the timeline is the record
of how it got there. They are separate on purpose.

One write is one event, however many fields it changes; a comment given with the write
belongs to that event, as does a page's edit summary. A write that changes nothing records no event.

An event belongs to the issue or page written to, and also appears on the timeline of every
issue or page whose parent or blocking edges it changed, or that it unblocked or blocked
again. Closing a blocker shows on each dependent it frees; moving a page shows on its old
and new parent. A **mention** does not carry an event onto the mentioned issue or page —
the backlink appears, the timeline stays quiet.

The event names **who** by the surface and client that made the write (an agent through
MCP, the CLI, the web UI), not by a person.

An issue's or page's **updated** time is the time of the latest event on its timeline — a comment or
a claim updates an issue as much as a title change does.

## Ready

An issue is **ready** when it is open, unblocked, and unclaimed — work anyone could take
right now.

Consumers may have their own word for a scoped slice of ready work (wayfinder calls its
version the *frontier*); cloisters does not adopt those words.

ADR 0001: Hand-roll MCP as a Ring handler

# Hand-roll MCP as a Ring handler instead of adopting a library

Status: accepted, 2026-10-25.

MCP is cloisters' primary interface, and its contract needs both the stateless 2026-07-28 revision (which Claude Code
negotiates) and 2025-11-25, tool handlers that see the request URL and client name, and `isError` results carrying
`structuredContent`. As of October 2026 no Clojure library speaks 2026-07-28 (PluMCP 0.3.0 lists it as TODO;
roklenarcic/mcp-server 0.3.61 is alpha and quiet), and the only JVM implementation that does, the Java SDK's 2.2.0-M1
milestone, is a servlet plus Reactor that mounts beside a Ring stack, not inside it. So cloisters implements MCP itself:
a Ring handler at `/mcp` from JSON-RPC request maps to response maps, JSON responses only, tools only, with the official
conformance suite run in CI at both revisions as the safety net. Tikka's equivalent was about 200 lines.

## Consequences

Cloisters owns spec drift: each new revision is its own work, and the conformance suite says when it falls behind.
That stays cheap only while the contract refuses everything hard in MCP (resources, prompts, sampling, elicitation,
tasks, subscriptions, auth).

**Revisit when** a Clojure MCP library supports both current revisions, gives tool handlers the request and client
info, and publishes conformance results (PluMCP is the likeliest), or when the contract grows beyond tools.

## Build conventions from the skeleton

These go into `CLAUDE.md` in M0. The detail is in
[Walking skeleton](../.wayfinder/tickets/T13-walking-skeleton.md).

- Write malli schemas with `mu/merge`, not `:merge`. Write titles as a single `:re`, not
  `[:and :string [:re …]]`.
- In HoneySQL raw fragments, bind parameters with `[:lift x]`; `RETURNING` allocates ids.
- The CLI sends `Host: 127.0.0.1:<port>`; the hardening allows both `localhost` and `127.0.0.1`.
- Write `java.lang.ProcessHandle` and other newer `java.lang` classes fully qualified.
- The service unit keeps `--enable-native-access=ALL-UNNAMED`.
